papers.Title: CAMI: A Counselor Agent Supporting Motivational Interviewing through State Inference and Topic Exploration

values.Temporal_Modeling_Details: The client simulator uses a state transition module based on the transtheoretical model of health behavior change with three states (Precontemplation, Contemplation, Preparation). The client starts in Precontemplation state and transitions to Contemplation only when the counselor's utterances mention the client's motivations, as determined by analyzing counselor utterances. A dynamic engagement module adjusts the client's engagement level based on the topic distance between the counselor's current topic and the client's ground truth motivation topic, using four levels of distance derived from the topic tree. An action selection module uses session context and the client's receptivity score to sample appropriate actions from a receptivity-aware action distribution, preventing overly compliant behavior.

papers.Title: AgentClinic: a multimodal agent benchmark to evaluate AI in simulated clinical environments

values.Temporal_Modeling_Details: Doctor agents are limited to N=20 interaction turns before a diagnosis must be made. The Notebook tool enables experiential learning that persists across patient cases—agents can write, edit, and retrieve Notes from prior interactions to improve future diagnostic performance. Biases are introduced via system prompts that persistently affect agent behavior throughout the dialogue. Experiments vary interaction time (N=10, 15, 20, 25, 30) to test the effect of limited vs. extended interaction on diagnostic accuracy.
values.Raw Eval Metrics: Diagnostic accuracy, Patient confidence (1-10), Patient compliance (1-10), Patient consultation rating (1-10), Normalized accuracy (Accuracybias/AccuracyNo Bias), Clinician ratings for Doctor realism, Patient realism, Measurement realism, and Empathy (1-10)
